script.title: Loss Aversion: Why Losing 20 Dollars Hurts Twice as Much
script.hook: Why does losing twenty dollars hurt twice as much as finding it?

scenes.text: Why does losing twenty dollars hurt twice as much as finding it?
Your brain is hardwired with a cognitive bias called loss aversion.
Nobel Prize winning research proved that pain from loss feels twice as intense as joy from gain.
Evolution shaped this survival reaction millions of years ago.
For early humans, losing food meant death, while gaining food was just a bonus.
Today, marketers exploit this exact fear using limited time deals.
You are not buying to gain something, you are buying to avoid losing it.
